 Jrue Holiday provided a boost off the bench with 17 points (7-of-11 FGs), eight rebounds, 10 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers against the Nuggets on Monday.
 Holiday didn’t step into the starting unit when Ja Morant (hamstring) went down, but he did step up off the bench in this game. He fell shy of the triple-double, but he did set season highs for both rebounds and assists in the win. Portland is now 5-1 this season, and Holiday has been a big part of their early success. He should continue to see a boost in production off the bench until Morant returns.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Scoot Henderson 
 POR

 Scoot Henderson tallied 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), three rebounds, one assist, three steals and one three-pointer in Saturday’s win over the Jazz. 
 As expected, Henderson replaced Ja Morant (hamstring) in the starting lineup on Saturday. Unfortunately, he produced one assist and four turnovers in 31 minutes, but his steals tally was solid. Jrue Holiday (14/4/3/1 with two three-pointers) played nine fewer minutes than Henderson and was the more efficient of the two. Henderson is worth rostering while Morant sits, but those who add him will likely have to accept the efficiency issues. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Ja Morant has been diagnosed with a Grade 2 left hamstring strain and will miss at least four weeks. 
 Morant sustained the injury on Thursday against his former team, and it will cost him the next month, at minimum. Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday should see the most run in Morant’s absence, but it’s not yet known which of the pair will start alongside Damian Lillard. 
 Ja Morant 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Ja Morant (hamstring) will not return to Thursday’s game against the Grizzlies. 
 Morant was ruled out more than halfway through the fourth quarter, and they pulled the starters a couple minutes later. This could have been precautionary, but the team should provide more of an update in the coming days. Scoot Henderson and Jrue Holiday should take on more minutes if Morant misses time, with Jrue likely starting. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Jrue Holiday recorded 22 points (8-of-12 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Lakers. 
 After totaling 20 points in Portland’s first two games, Holiday had his most productive night of the season on Tuesday. The veteran guard played 30 minutes off the bench, and his minutes have increased in each of Portland’s three games. Thirty minutes may be Holiday’s cap, not because of health, but because of Portland’s perimeter depth. Starters Damian Lillard and Ja Morant also played at least 30 minutes, with fellow reserve Scoot Henderson logging 17. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Jrue Holiday with 12 points (4-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists, a steal, a block and three 3-pointers on Friday against the Kings. 
 Jrue played 26 minutes in this game and played very well despite not having the stat line that would reflect how good he was. The Blazers went small and Jrue kept coming up big. While his fantasy upside is capped with Ja Morant and Damian Lillard back on the team, he should still be able to do bits and pieces to remain relevant in most fantasy redraft leagues. 
 Deni Avdija 
 POR 
 Forward 
 #8 
 Deni Avdija (ankle) is questionable to play against the Suns on Wednesday. 
 Avdija looked good during the preseason, but there is a chance he is sidelined for Portland’s regular season opener. Portland’s thin on the wing, with Vít Krejčí next in line on the depth chart. It’s possible the Trail Blazers use three guards in the starting unit instead of starting Krejčí, which would likely mean Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday all start. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Jrue Holiday finished Monday’s exhibition against the London Lions with six points (3-of-5 FGs), five rebounds and three assists. 
 Damian Lillard didn’t play in Monday’s exhibition, and his absence opened a starting spot for Holiday. Like the other starters, the veteran guard was done at halftime. The move to the bench lowers Holiday’s fantasy ceiling considerably, giving managers no reason to use a top-100 pick on him. However, he should play enough to provide reliable late-round value in most leagues. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Jrue Holiday finished Wednesday’s exhibition against the Warriors with five points (2-of-8 FGs), seven rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer. 
 Holiday came off the bench in Wednesday’s preseason opener, as expected. The good news for fantasy managers is that the veteran guard still provided positive value in rebounds and assists. Coming off the bench does lower Holiday’s fantasy ceiling considerably, pushing his ADP outside the first 100 picks in 12-team leagues. He’ll be worth a look for managers hoping to add a “safer” option in the latter rounds of drafts. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 NBA Insider Jake Fischer reports Jrue Holiday is not in talks with the Trail Blazers about securing a buyout. 
 Despite rumors that Holiday would join the 76ers after securing a buyout, Portland intends to keep him around. Holiday appeared in 53 games for the Trail Blazers last season, averaging 16.3 points, 4.6 rebounds, 6.1 assists and a career-high 2.6 three-pointers per game. With Ja Morant now in town and Damian Lillard healthy, it’s unclear what Holiday’s role will be, but he should see plenty of minutes as one of the best defenders on the team. 
 Jrue Holiday 
 POR 
 Guard 
 #5 
 Jrue Holiday tallied 20 points (6-of-13 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s Game 4 loss to the Spurs. 
 Eleven of Portland’s 18 turnovers in Game 4 were committed by two players. Holiday racked up six, while Deni Avdija was responsible for five. Holiday was solid as a scorer, shooting 3-of-6 from beyond the arc, but the mistakes were too much to overcome as the Spurs turned up the dial defensively in the second half. Holiday has scored at least 20 points in consecutive games, but he’ll need to be more efficient as a playmaker if the Trail Blazers are to force a Game 6.

 De’Anthony Melton finished Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets with 11 points (3-of-7 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one block and three three-pointers.
 Melton’s final stat line wasn’t much to write home about, but his role may expand for Friday’s game against the Spurs. Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury and is expected to undergo an MRI on Thursday. If Curry misses time, Melton will have a larger role, whether he moves into the starting lineup or continues to come off the bench.

 Brandin Podziemski accounted for 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, four assists, two steals and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets.
 For the first time this season, Podziemski has scored at least 20 points in consecutive games. He finished with a solid stat line, missing only a blocked shot. And the Warriors may need even more from Podziemski in the short term, as Stephen Curry left Wednesday’s game with an abdominal injury.

 Yaxel Lendeborg amassed 25 points (9-of-19 FGs, 5-of-8 FTs), 10 rebounds, two steals and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Rockets.
 Lendeborg has scored at least 25 points in six games this season. Against the Rockets, he shouldered more of the offensive workload after Stephen Curry (core) exited, finishing with his third double-double. Through 12 games, only Wilt Chamberlain and Rick Barry have scored more points as a rookie in Warriors history than Lendeborg. The Warriors visit the Spurs on Friday in what will be another challenging matchup for Yaxel, especially if Curry can’t play.

 Fred VanVleet finished Wednesday’s win over the Warriors with 18 points (6-of-9 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, three steals and four three-pointers.
 “Steady Freddie” has been the calming influence the Rockets lacked last season while he was recovering from an ACL tear. Against the Warriors, VanVleet shot 66.7 percent from the field and posted solid numbers in assists, steals and three-pointers. VanVleet is currently providing top-100 fantasy value, and that’s closer to his floor than his ceiling.

 Thompson remains a valuable fantasy option, especially for managers willing to punt three-pointers. However, his scoring average has decreased by more than three points per game compared to last season. Thompson’s ability to fill a stat line has preserved most of his value.  In 10 games this season, Şengün has recorded six double-doubles and one triple-double. His fantasy value has also been boosted by improved efficiency, with the Rockets center shooting over 50 percent from the field and posting higher averages in points, rebounds, and assists. Turnovers can still be an issue for Şengün on occasion, but he committed just two against the Warriors.

 Kevin Durant shot 8-of-17 from the field and 3-of-4 from the foul line in Wednesday’s win over the Warriors, scoring 20 points with four rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer.
 Durant led six Rockets in double figures on Wednesday, and he’s scored at least 20 points in four straight games. Given his career résumé, that isn’t a significant achievement for KD. That said, he’s been more aggressive offensively than he was earlier in the season, which is good for those rostering Durant.

 Darryn Peterson got himself 22 points (7-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, a steal, a block, and two 3-pointers in 123-108 loss to the Magic. 
 Over the past week, Darryn Peterson has gotten more confident, aggressive, and the Jazz have been letting him lose. The peripheral stats from college have started to come back, and it’s been exciting to watch. You want more in terms of efficiency, but with Lauri Markkanen out for a month, Darryn is a must roster if he hasn’t been picked up in your league already.

 Ace Bailey put up 18 points (6-of-17 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), seven rebounds, two assists, two steals, four blocks, and three 3-pointers in loss on Wednesday. 
 Ace Bailey has been great this season and has been one of the best shot blockers in the NBA. His ability to havoc defender at this point is a great sign for his long-term development. He’s coachable and is a great teammate. The efficiency wasn’t great in this one, but it’s hard to complain with the peripheral stats that he gave you in this one.
